correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3 and threshold-one synchronous 3-state Greenberg–Hastings dynamics on C_n square K2, apply Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff finite-graph Theorem 3: extinction iff the integer edge 1-form g(a,b)=1_(a,b)=(0,1)-1_(a,b)=(1,0) has zero cycle circulation. n square faces plus one rim generate the integer cycle lattice (rank n+1). Build the 9-state rung Laurent matrix from zero square curl, impose one independent upper-rim winding by [z^0]tr M(z)^n. Direct symbolic 9x9 computation independently confirms det(xI-M(1))=(x-2)^3(x+1)^4(x²-7x+4) and second log-weight derivative -2(x-2)(x+1)^2(3x³+21x-16), giving lambda=(7+sqrt33)/2 and sigma²>0. A zero-weight self loop and weight-one allowed 3-cycle show unique Fourier maximal phase, eliminating other saddle contributions and proving Gaussian local limit n^-1/2 with one winding constraint. Independent Laurent dynamic programming yields E_3=261,E_4=1485,E_5=8409,E_6=49215. Finite checks do not prove all-n asymptotics; primitive PF perturbation and Fourier steepest descent do.
